headline: 綠洲重聚、馬斯克紀錄片登場
context: 英倫搖滾天團 Oasis 重聚巡演的紀錄片《Don't Look Back in Anger》本週上線，片中收錄了 Liam 與 Noel Gallagher 首次排練時的緊張氣氛，還有兩兄弟私下聊政治的畫面，但完全沒提到票價這件事。另一邊，紀錄片名導艾力克斯・吉布尼（Alex Gibney）執導的馬斯克（Elon Musk）紀錄片也同步登場，內容談到他的商業交易、早期理想主義，以及想生一大堆孩子的野心。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Capturing the band’s 2025 global comeback tour, this two-hour film reveals the tense first rehearsal with Liam, Noel being a big softie and the Gallaghers’ politics – just don’t expect any mention of ticket prices It was the reunion that many thought would never happen: Oasis re-forming for a series of sold-out live shows, their first since Noel and Liam Gallagher split acrimoniously in 2009. For those who managed to get tickets last year, the performances were a celebration of one of Britpop’s finest bands and a chance to live through a night of 90s nostalgia. For the millions who missed out, be it due to demand or budgetary restraints, the tour represented a generational Fomo moment. Luckily, the directors Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern were embedded within team Oasis throughout the whole thing, alongside the Peaky Blinders creator, Steven Knight: the result is Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger , a two-hour concert film that hits cinemas around the world this week. Whether you were on the front row at Manchester’s Heaton Park, doing the Poznan in Seoul or stuck at home watching it all online, Don’t Look Back in Anger captures the Oasis Live ’25 Tour for posterity. Here’s what we learned. Continue reading...
sources.title: Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger: what we learned from the year’s biggest rockumentary

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children Veteran documentarian Alex Gibney’s film about the richest broligarch on the planet has been one of the most eagerly anticipated films at the Venice film festival this year. The Oscar-winning 72-year-old, who has in previous films taken on the US military, the Catholic church, Vladimir Putin and Scientology, has been investigating the tech tycoon’s ascent and speaking to people in his orbit since late 2022, before his Maga turn and Trump 2.0. The result clocks in at just under four hours and presents a comprehensive answer to how on earth one man managed to amass so much money and political influence. It is shocking less for any individual new pieces of information Gibney has unearthed than for its totality. Here are six things the film tells us: Continue reading...
sources.title: State handouts, 10,000 lasers – and Trump’s election: six things we learned from the Elon Musk film

thread_text:
